solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lacking money for a sweet treat

parts.note: to be short of something is to lack it
bread is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone too broke to buy themselves a little something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking money' reads as one idea, being broke, but each word does its own job; bread is long-standing slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich, crumbly Scottish biscuit, a classic sugary teatime indulgence.

clue.text: Wander off course, having drunk lagers and G&T

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of gin and tonic's abbreviation, G and T

explanation.surface: A drinker veers off the path after a session of lager and gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the past tense of drink in the story, but it tells you to rearrange LAGERS with G and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To straggle is to stray or trail away from the main group or the intended route.

clue.text: Shop's wrapping present, perhaps a marble

indicators.note: the wrapping of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of shop are used

parts.note: the outside letters of shop are S and P
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A shop gift-wrapping a present, which might be a marble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that a marble is just one example of the answer; the 's of Shop's is possessive, so its wrapping is S and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A marble is a small glass ball, an example of a round solid shape.

clue.text: Gate at the front opens outwards for convenience

parts.note: a portal is a gateway or doorway

indicators.note: the front of each of the next two words is taken, their opening letters only

parts.note: first letter of opens
first letter of outwards

explanation.surface: A gate positioned at the front of a property that swings outward.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'convenience' is the British euphemism for a public toilet; a Portaloo is a portable cabin toilet seen at festivals and building sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Public convenience is a polite British term for a toilet, and a Portaloo is a brand of portable one.

clue.text: Make firm edict on EU policy, essentially

indicators.note: at its essence, inside the phrase, the letters are found across the words edict on EU policy

explanation.surface: A government issuing a strong decree on European Union policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone up is to make muscles or the body firmer through exercise.

clue.text: Measure of speed for computing performance a failure

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: A benchmark of computing performance turns out to be a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computing performance' reads as one phrase, but 'performance' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigaflop is a billion floating-point operations per second, a unit for rating processor speed.

clue.text: Making large pants, wife certainly lacking energy once

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped
once means one time only, so just one of the two Es in the word is removed

parts.note: indeed means certainly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A wife enlarging some underpants, apparently with little energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but means gasps for breath; INDEED loses only one of its two Es, as 'once' insists.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone winded is out of breath, gasping heavily after a blow or exertion.

clue.text: Aware of current option in a French referendum?

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
non is French for no, one of the two answers on a ballot

explanation.surface: Someone well informed about the choices in a vote held in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in on something is to share knowledge of it, such as a secret or a plan.

clue.text: A little bit of sushi taken, certainly no turkey!

indicators.note: only a small piece of the words sushi taken is used, the letters spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone at a meal has sampled the sushi, but definitely not any turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A turkey is slang for a flop, so something that is certainly not one is a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is a failed show or film; its opposite is a big success.

clue.text: Expert getting job offer

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a position is a job or post

explanation.surface: A skilled professional receives a job offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job offer' reads as one phrase, but 'job' belongs to the wordplay and 'offer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition is a proposal or suggested deal put to someone.

clue.text: Rob no longer taking ecstasy in wild party

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the party word holds the drug letter

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A thief has gone straight, giving up crime for drugs at raves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks the word as archaic: it once meant to rob or plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Reave is an obsolete verb meaning to plunder or carry off by force.

clue.text: Trollope's work — according to Basil Fawlty, something not to mention and study

parts.words: according to Basil Fawlty, something not to mention
parts.note: Basil Fawlty, in the sitcom Fawlty Towers, famously says 'Don't mention the war'
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question blending a Victorian novel with a classic TV catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s BBC sitcom; Basil Fawlty, its hotelier, keeps telling staff not to mention the war in front of German guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Warden is Anthony Trollope's 1855 novel, the first of his Barsetshire series.

clue.text: So what British model keeps in bottom of bag

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an ideal is a perfect model

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in this down-style reading is its last letter

explanation.surface: A shrug at a British fashion model keeping something at the bottom of her bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Big deal is a sarcastic retort meaning something is unimportant, much like who cares.

clue.text: Boy cutting French bread for knight

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy slicing a French loaf to feed a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's twelve peers, hence any chivalrous champion.

clue.text: Fan of Hayek and Friedman provoked a rebellion

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A free-market economist's admirer stirring up a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Friedrich Hayek and Milton Friedman were leading free-market economists.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoliberal favours free markets and minimal state intervention, as those economists advocated.

clue.text: Music maker possibly making EP?

indicators.note: possibly making asks which words could be shortened to give the letters that follow

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail, and P is the musical abbreviation for piano, so the two words abbreviate to these letters

explanation.surface: A musician wondering if this instrument could record an extended-play disc.
explanation.walkthrough: EP looks like a short record, but it is what the answer's two words abbreviate to.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic piano is a keyboard instrument that produces sound electronically.

clue.text: Dimness shown by idiot not finishing crossword answer

indicators.note: not finishing means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a twit is an idiot
a light is the word entered in a crossword grid

explanation.surface: A fool who can't complete the puzzle shows how dim he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the half-dark between day and night, a state of dimness.

clue.text: Water bug needing temperature to be good

indicators.note: needing a change, one letter of the word must be swapped
to be marks what the named letter becomes in its place

parts.note: to bug is to irritate

explanation.surface: A gardener's insect pest that needs warmth to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water bug' looks like an insect, but 'Water' is the definition and 'bug' the verb irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land or crops with water.

clue.text: Recover, following American doctor with unprincipled approach

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this word is placed after the others

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to rally is to recover

explanation.surface: A patient recovers under an American doctor with dubious ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorally means without any moral sense, acting without principles.

clue.text: Refuse some cocaine after the end of the year

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: Dec, December, is the year's final month
a line is a single dose of cocaine laid out to snort

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a line of cocaine at a New Year party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of the year' means the last month, not the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to say no to an invitation or offer.

clue.text: Rodents playing hard to get with Manx cat

parts.note: coy describes someone who feigns shyness

indicators.note: the Manx cat has no tail, so the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Rodents feigning shyness in front of a cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Coypus are large South American water rodents, also called nutria.

clue.text: Imagine one's lost, cracking cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: lost means gone, so the letter for one is missing from the word
cracking means breaking up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone imagining they are lost while trying to crack a cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from IMAGINE to leave MAGINE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling.

clue.text: Recipe with sauce smothering very Italian food

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions

indicators.note: smothering means covering, so the sauce wraps around the letter

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise sauce

explanation.surface: A cookbook dish where the sauce is thoroughly smothering something Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, a staple of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Promising outstanding victory at first

indicators.note: at first means just the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: outstanding means still owing, unpaid

explanation.surface: A promising athlete with a remarkable win early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Vowing means making a solemn promise.

clue.text: Broadcaster in sport simulating daredevil activity

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
in football, diving is faking a foul by falling over

explanation.surface: A TV broadcaster covering a sport where players fake injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British pay-TV broadcaster; a footballer who dives fakes being fouled.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydiving is jumping from an aircraft and freefalling before opening a parachute, a thrill-seeker's pursuit.

clue.text: Cover of Shakira by quiet band

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, first and last letters

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet band releasing a cover version of a Shakira song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version and 'band' a group, but the answer is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Good swimmer in the drink by Weymouth on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside letters of the word are removed

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A strong swimmer out in the sea off the resort of Weymouth during the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' looks like slang for the sea, but here it is beer; Weymouth is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are huge marine mammals perfectly built for life in the ocean.

clue.text: Relegated team's pot shot, playing with Man U

indicators.note: playing means in play or in motion, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A struggling football club takes a speculative shot against Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is Manchester United; Southampton were relegated from the Premier League in 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: Southampton FC dropped out of England's top football division at the end of the 2022-23 season.

clue.text: Grassland in spring, gently getting cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a leap is a spring or jump
P is piano, the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A meadow in springtime having its grass mown with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or open pasture.
